answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making every new identity earn standing via a supervised apprenticeship: each newcomer is paired with one established agent mentoring a single apprentice per epoch, and the apprentice must finish a chain of graded jobs before transacting freely. The starting point is a juniper ledge, narrow, exposed, where one failed job sends the apprentice back to the start. Mentorship slots are scarce and tied to real agents' time, so fake identities only lengthen the queue, and no money buys a shortcut past the work, so the nebula of anonymous accounts thins out.
